items.performers: Steve Reich Ensemble; Steve Reich (piano, marimba)
items.label: ECM Records
items.note: Eleven chords support a steady beat from pianos and mallet instruments, while voices and clarinets phrase by the length of a breath. Reich played piano and marimba on his ensemble’s 1976 New York recording, released in 1978, and James Preiss played the metallophone signals that move the group from one section to the next. It remains the recording to start with.

items.performers: Kronos Quartet (David Harrington, John Sherba, Hank Dutt, Joan Jeanrenaud)
items.label: Nonesuch
items.note: Strings imitate the recorded speech of Reich’s governess, a Pullman porter and three Holocaust survivors, against train sounds from America and Europe. Kronos recorded the work in San Francisco before giving its première in London in 1988. The 1989 album, the first recording of both works, couples it with Electric Counterpoint, which Pat Metheny recorded in New York in 1987; each sets live players against recordings of themselves.

items.label: Deutsche Grammophon
items.note: A single bongo stroke is built up into a twelve-beat pattern that passes through marimbas, glockenspiels and voices. Reich played in his own ensemble on this 85-minute recording of the complete work, made at Polydor Studios, Hamburg, in January 1974; Cornelius Cardew was among the players, and Joan La Barbara and Jay Clayton sang. The set adds two 1973 scores, Six Pianos and Music for Mallet Instruments, Voices and Organ.
